title: Non-blocking follow-ups from PR #158 review (frontend-divergence-markers)
description: Tracked non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #158 (frontend-divergence-markers), recorded here per CLAUDE.md's 'every non-blocking finding becomes a tracked task' rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges. Distinct from the PR's own blocking finding (the divergence overlay distorting the chart's time axis when the currently selected range doesn't include the divergence's own dates), which stays on frontend-divergence-markers itself and must be fixed before that PR can be accepted.

checklist.step: OscillatorChart.tsx's divergence overlay is built inside the single chart-creation `useEffect` (which now also depends on `divergence`), so the whole multi-pane oscillator chart is torn down and rebuilt from scratch (visible flicker, lost zoom/pan/crosshair state) whenever `analysisQuery.data` resolves after `indicatorsQuery.data` -- purely to add two marker points. PriceChart.tsx avoids this by keeping its own divergence overlay in a separate effect that only adds/removes series on the existing chart/series refs (gated on `chartRef.current`/`seriesRef.current` already being set). Consider the same separate-effect treatment for OscillatorChart.tsx, consistent with how PriceChart.tsx already splits its own signal-overlay/zone-overlay/divergence-overlay effects.

The bullish/bearish `label`/`position` derivation (`divergence.kind === 'bullish' ? 'Bullish divergence' : 'Bearish divergence'` / `belowBar`/`aboveBar`) is copy-pasted verbatim between `buildDivergencePriceOverlay` (PriceChart.tsx) and `buildDivergenceIndicatorOverlay` (OscillatorChart.tsx), even though the PR already factored out the one other genuinely shared piece of divergence logic (`clickedDivergenceExtreme` in divergenceClick.ts). Consider factoring this into a shared helper (e.g. alongside `clickedDivergenceExtreme` in divergenceClick.ts) so a future change to the label wording or up/down convention can't leave the two charts silently out of sync.

decisions.decision: Split OscillatorChart.tsx's divergence overlay (line series, markers, click subscription) into its own `useEffect`, separate from the chart-creation effect -- gated on `chartRef.current` already being set by the chart-creation effect, mirroring PriceChart.tsx's own per-overlay effect pattern (including its 'skip cleanup if the chart was already disposed' ref-equality guard). Also factored the duplicated bullish/bearish label/position derivation into a new `divergenceMarkerLabelAndPosition` helper in divergenceClick.ts, used by both PriceChart.tsx's `buildDivergencePriceOverlay` and OscillatorChart.tsx's `buildDivergenceIndicatorOverlay`. Implemented as part of a batched PR (task/frontend-followups-batch-1) alongside four other small stocks-page follow-up tasks.
decisions.rationale: Both fixes had a clear, already-established template to follow (PriceChart.tsx's own divergence-overlay effect and its 'skip cleanup' guard; divergenceClick.ts's existing `clickedDivergenceExtreme`/`isDivergenceInRange` as the precedent for where shared divergence logic lives), so there was no genuinely open design question -- just applying the same pattern OscillatorChart.tsx hadn't yet adopted. Added a new OscillatorChart.test.tsx test (mirroring PriceChart.test.tsx's own 'removes the previous divergence line/markers/click subscription and adds new ones when the divergence changes' test) to actually exercise the new effect's cleanup path, which the existing suite hadn't covered at all (confirmed via a coverage regression check before this fix -- lines 509-511 of the new effect were uncovered until that test was added).

review.notes: Reviewed as part of PR #207, a batched PR covering five followup tasks (this one plus frontend-trend-strength-chart-followups, frontend-volume-indicators-chart-followups, frontend-tide-region-chart-shading-followups, frontend-profit-target-display-followups); see this PR's own COMMENTED-type review for the full cross-task verification detail. This task's own change (splitting OscillatorChart.tsx's divergence overlay into its own effect, mirroring PriceChart.tsx) was specifically checked for the recurring bug classes this review pass targets: (1) z-order/occlusion -- live browser walkthrough on ADBE (whose divergence dates fall inside the default 1y range) confirmed the divergence line/markers render correctly on top of the Stochastic/RSI lines on both panes, matching the deterministic ordering the effect split guarantees (the chart-creation effect always completes and sets chartRef.current before the divergence effect's gated body runs, since React runs passive effects in declaration order within one commit); (2) stale closure / missing cleanup / wrong deps -- the new effect's dependency array ([indicatorsQuery.data, divergence, theme, enabled]) and its 'skip cleanup if chartRef.current !== chart' guard correctly mirror PriceChart.tsx's established pattern, and the new OscillatorChart.test.tsx test explicitly exercises the cleanup path (removeSeries/unsubscribeClick/detachMarkers all called exactly once on a divergence-only refetch, createChartMock NOT called again); (3) live click-to-explain -- clicked an actual divergence marker on ADBE's oscillator pane and confirmed the AnchoredInfoBalloon opened with the correct divergence explanation text, confirming subscribeClick still wires correctly post-refactor. Range-windowing edge case (switching to 1M, where ADBE's divergence falls out of range) confirmed the overlay is correctly skipped with no axis distortion, on both panes. No console errors or failed network requests throughout. Genuine fix for a real problem (full-chart teardown/flicker on an analysis-only refetch), no new bug introduced. No findings specific to this task's own change.
